feed.title: antxiko — commented disassemblies of 8-bit games
feed.subtitle: Old 8-bit binaries taken apart byte by byte and commented, with the tools to rebuild them: nothing gets claimed that the binary does not show, and the source has to give the original back, byte for byte. Right now that means 102 MSX games.

entry.title: Snatcher, taken apart: three disks, and a new section for Konami on disk
entry.summary: Konami's cyberpunk adventure for MSX2 (1988): its 4,320 sectors with their owners and the three disks rebuilt byte for byte. A map of the 251 scenes of the script (spoilers!), 154 pictures painted by the engine, 45 tunes played by its own driver and the debugger Konami left on disk 1. Uranai Sensation moves to the new section.

entry.title: Konami's Uranai Sensation, taken apart: the first disk
entry.summary: Konami's fortune teller for MSX2 (1988), the first disk in the series: every one of its 1,440 sectors with its owner and the disk rebuilt byte for byte. The screens painted by running the disk, the texts translated, how the blood-type percentage is worked out and where the omikuji's luck comes from.

entry.title: Youkai Yashiki: the bosses, the ending and the yokai type by type
entry.summary: The five events painted by running the game, each with its GIF; the girl of the ending; the 23 enemy types checked over 35,966 frames. Two new bugs. Thanks to Nestor Sancho.

entry.title: Youkai Yashiki: the 64 sprite drawings
entry.summary: Every drawing in the sprite table with the code that sets it; 0x90 is the only unused one. The pause, recorded. Thanks to Nestor Sancho.

entry.title: Eagle Fighter: the in-flight refuelling
entry.summary: The tanker that only comes from stage 3, forced in openMSX: it comes down, four warnings, the plane hooks on and fills up.

entry.title: Pachinko UFO: the slot machine spinning
entry.summary: The slot machine of the board, forced in openMSX, spins in a GIF: three digits, 0, 5 and 5, and no prize.

entry.title: Exciting Jockey: the nine whole tracks
entry.summary: Every race from the start to the finish, 1,200 to 3,600 metres, built by running the ROM column by column the way the track scrolls, with its bushes, signs, fences and water jumps.

entry.title: Ice World: the 52 maps
entry.summary: Every maze the game counts, built by running the ROM the way each stage starts, and checked against the seven recorded stages: all identical.

entry.title: Eagle Fighter: the sixteen stage screens
entry.summary: The screen every stage starts with, built by running the ROM: the game has no map, and what changes is the ground colour and the horizon, which repeat every eight stages. Checked against the two recorded stages.

entry.title: Exoide-Z Area 5: the whole map
entry.summary: The whole trip, all 81 positions, built by running the ROM in order on the same machine, with every change of tiles, and checked against the recording that goes through them all.

entry.title: Issun-boushi no Donnamondai: the maps of the five scenes
entry.summary: Each scene whole: the river as the game scrolls it (every row reversed) and the land where the oni waits, built by running the ROM and checked against the recordings.

entry.title: Youkai Yashiki: the plans of the places
entry.summary: Every screen of every place in its spot on the plan, built by running the ROM, including a sixth place reached by five doors that no recording had visited, and four screens that are on no plan.

entry.title: The Seal of Hades: the maps of the six scenes
entry.summary: The eleven screens of every scene, bottom to top, built by running the ROM with each screen tile set, and checked against the recording through the scrolling window.

entry.title: Iga Ninpouchou Mangetsu-jou: the maps of the seven stages
entry.summary: The bridge, the courtyard, the four castle floors and the boss tower, every screen built by running the ROM and checked against the recording: 9,255 of 10,958 aligned frames come out identical.

entry.title: Moai no Hihou: the maps of the 32 stages
entry.summary: All 32 stages whole, built by running the ROM the way the game builds them when the view scrolls, and checked against the recording: half of the recorded frames come out identical tile for tile.

entry.title: Koneko no Daibouken: the maps of the 18 stages
entry.summary: Every screen of every stage, built by running the ROM with the tiles of its scene, in three maps (one per town), checked against the recorded screens.

entry.title: Game Land: the texts
entry.summary: A new page with the 51 menus, 47 messages and the labels of the program, taken straight from the ROM and translated; the arrows in the menus turn out to be the cartridge own drawings.

entry.title: Issun-boushi no Donnamondai: the texts
entry.summary: A new page with every text in the ROM, where the code writes it and its translation, from the CASIO intro to どんなもんだい in the ending.

entry.title: Casio World Open: the swing, played
entry.summary: The golfer swing recorded in openMSX: the frame changes every 8 frames, and the top of the backswing only shows if the power goes past 0x40. Two GIFs on the front page, every recorded frame checked against the pieces the ROM gives for it.

entry.title: Koneko no Daibouken: the hidden screens, played
entry.summary: The two screens behind the goal house, now in openMSX: a hook on the screen change sends the kitten past the house on 2-2 and 3-3, and the game scrolls in the log in the meadow and the waterfall with their enemies. Two new GIFs, checked against the screens built from the ROM.
